text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate and connection resets detected for inference traffic routed to us-east-1a (control-plane and data-plane path). Source: synthetic probes + customer telemetry. Investigating.

maria-sre: I’m on it. Looking at LB healthers and host-level NIC errors. Initial signal looks like a subset of instances in us-east-1a are dropping established connections (EPIPE/Econnreset) while CPU/GPU appear fine.

alex-runtime: seeing repeated `socket: recvfrom: connection reset by peer` in runtime logs for model-serving pods pinned to us-east-1a hosts. KV cache misses spike too. Rolling degrade starting ~2123456500

priya-platform: Alarms: request latency p50->p95 gap increased and error-rate to 5xx crossed 3% threshold. Customers with Dedicated pools in us-east-1a reporting elevated tail latency. Paging oncall.

oncall-bob: Got page. What’s the blast radius? Are we seeing API gateway errors or only inference path? Customer impact severity? cc @chloe-support

chloe-support: Ticket churn: three support tickets from mid-market customers in the last 12m, complaining about timeouts on generation and aborted streams. No reported data loss; mainly degraded UX.

maria-sre: Blast radius: internal synthetic probes hitting hosted-api endpoints routed to us-east-1a, plus Dedicated customers pinned to us-east-1a pools. Not global yet. No control-plane-wide errors but routes anchored to 1a are affected.

tim-eng-infra: I’m pulling host metrics from the AZ. Not seeing CPU/GPU saturation. I do see elevated interface error counts on a subset of ENIs on hosts provisioned in 1a. Could be a host-side NIC firmware bug or AWS network plane issue.

alex-runtime: Suggest failing over routing for inference traffic away from us-east-1a while infra investigates. We can set a soft avoid route for 1a and re-route Dedicated pools to other AZs/regions.

priya-platform: Can we do a controlled reroute? We should avoid mass reboots. Plan: (1) set routing policy to prefer other AZs/regions for new requests, (2) enable fallback for pinned Dedicated pools to move to us-east-1b if capacity available, (3) for customers who explicitly pinned, notify support.

maria-sre: Agreed. Setting emergency route policy now: `redwoodctl route update --region us-east-1 --avoid-az=1a --grace-period=30s`

ops-bot: COMMAND RUN: redwoodctl route update --region us-east-1 --avoid-az=1a --grace-period=30s

ops-bot: OK: Route policy updated, new requests will prefer other AZs. Existing sticky sessions will be allowed to drain for 30s.

alex-runtime: Pushing fallback model variant for latency-critical endpoints so customers still get responses even if larger model has transient failures. Will update canary rules.

maria-sre: Starting host-level cordon for the worst-affected nodes to stop new allocations: `ssh infra@host && sudo systemctl stop redwood-agent` (do not reboot yet). We'll keep them available for diagnostics.

tim-eng-infra: Cordon commands issued on 4 hosts. Draining pods from those hosts. Monitoring for impact on capacity.

priya-platform: Auto-scaling triggered to compensate for capacity loss; spun up extra instances in us-east-1b and us-east-1c. ETA ~2m for new nodes to be ready for traffic.

chloe-support: Drafting customer message for affected Dedicated customers: will advise degraded inference in us-east-1a with active failover, ask customers not to pin to 1a during mitigation. Share for approval.

maria-sre: Observability: packet drop metrics at host NICS spiked, AWS did not report zone-wide outage yet. Opening AWS support case (severity 1). Case ID: 1234567890 (submitted).

oncall-bob: Any signs of DNS flaps or resolver issues? That changed previous incidents.

alex-runtime: No DNS errors in stack; connections established then reset. So likely network path at host or hypervisor level. But continue to monitor DNS to be safe.

priya-platform: We should also flip routing for certain circuits to cross-region fallback for heavy long-tail requests. Adding rule: `redwoodctl route set --policy cross-region-fallback=on --latency-sla=200ms`

maria-sre: Cross-region fallback rule applied.

ops-bot: COMMAND RUN: redwoodctl route set --policy cross-region-fallback=on --latency-sla=200ms

tim-eng-infra: AWS case update: fabric team acknowledged elevated packet drops for a subset of hosts in us-east-1a; they’re isolating impacted hypervisors. ETA unknown.

alex-runtime: Runtime telemetry shows error-rate returning toward baseline for traffic that was shifted out of 1a. User-visible errors decreasing. Keep monitoring for sticky sessions.

maria-sre: Marking incident as partial mitigation achieved. Continuing to watch for reappearance. Keeping the cordon in place for now.

chloe-support: Customer comms sent to impacted Dedicated customers (copy pasted): "We're seeing degraded inference in us-east-1a. We've routed traffic away from impacted hosts and are monitoring. If you're pinned to 1a and need urgent assistance, reply to this thread." Responses expected.

oncall-bob: If AWS resolves quickly we can uncordon. If not, we should plan for moving persistent Dedicated workloads to alternate AZs and offer credits for SLA impact. Priya, please prepare options.

priya-platform: Preparing migrations for Dedicated tenants: cold-move steps + estimated downtime per tenant. Will post playbook in a few mins.

maria-sre: Postmortem notes so far: probable root cause: host NIC/network path degradation in us-east-1a causing econnreset; immediate mitigation: route avoidance + cordon + Dedicated fallback. Need follow-up items: add ENI error alerting, implement automatic avoid-az on sustained interface errors, improve customer notification templates.

tim-eng-infra: AWS updated case: they’ve isolated hypervisors and are doing live remediation. Hosts show reduced interface errors after interventions. They recommend we keep cordon until they finish.

alex-runtime: Re-enabling reduced-traffic test to verify KV-cache warmups in other AZs. All good so far.

maria-sre: Current status: degraded -> mitigated. Keeping incident channel open until AWS confirms full host health and we uncordon. Next actions: write up internal incident timeline, ops checklist for Dedicated migrations, and run a simulation to ensure automatic reroute works as intended.

chloe-support: I’ll queue a follow-up customer update in 30m with current status and timeline.

oncall-bob: Thx all for quick responses. I’m initiating post-incident ticket for RCA and compensation options. Will handoff to the day-shift SREs in 45m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=mitigated, notes=traffic rerouted; cordon in place; AWS investigating. Next update in 30 minutes or on any significant change."
